population_one_line: Adult inpatients with positive blood cultures (988 positive bottles from 7367 patients, 13.4% positivity) at a single UK hospital
ttp_reported: Median TII (time in incubator = TTP equivalent) 12.27h (IQR 7.42-19.88); median RPT (request-to-positivity) 23.63h (IQR not given); reported overall and by organism group in Tables 1-2
outcome_one_line: 30-day mortality 15.6% (130/834 with mortality data available); among clinically significant bacteraemias n=63 died within 30 days; RPT not associated with 30-day mortality (p=0.404)
notes: Previously excluded because transit time (not TTP) was the prognostic exposure. Under inclusive criteria, TII is functionally TTP and is reported as a median with IQR alongside 30-day mortality for the same BSI cohort. Authors explicitly tested RPT vs mortality (null). Useful for TTP distribution + mortality rate in a bacteraemia cohort.

population_one_line: Adult ICU patients with CR-BSI (37 standard vs 16 conservative diagnostic method) in a Brazilian tertiary hospital, 2000-2008
ttp_reported: Differential time to positivity (DTP) >2h used as cutpoint for the conservative CR-BSI diagnostic criterion; absolute TTP values not reported as a continuous variable
outcome_one_line: In-hospital mortality 57% (standard) vs 75% (conservative), p=0.208; ICU mortality and 24h-stratified subgroup mortality also reported
notes: Per instructions: TTP (DTP >120 min) is used as a CRBSI definitional inclusion criterion rather than a measured prognostic variable, so the TTP measurement is contaminated. Population (CR-BSI ICU cohort) + mortality rate are extractable; do NOT use as TTP-outcome evidence.

population_one_line: Adults with Staphylococcus lugdunensis bacteremia (12 multiple-positive, 37 single-positive sets) at a Japanese university hospital over 10 years
ttp_reported: Median TTP 21h (IQR 17-31) overall; 22h single-positive vs 20h multiple-positive (p=0.426); TTP <20h in 41.5%; cutpoint and continuous data both reported
outcome_one_line: 30-day mortality 13.3% (single) vs 18.2% (multiple); 90-day 36.7% vs 18.2%; persistent bacteremia 3.3% vs 18.2%
notes: Previously excluded because outcomes stratified by culture-set status rather than TTP. Under inclusive criteria, TTP median+IQR and TTP<20h cutpoint are reported for the cohort alongside 30/90-day mortality and persistent bacteremia rates. Both single- and multiple-positive subgroups extractable.

population_one_line: Hemodialysis patients with blood culture-positive BSI receiving adjunctive Seraph 100 hemoperfusion (first-in-human prospective interventional study, 4 German centers)
ttp_reported: TTP measured pre- and post-Seraph filter; median TTP increase 36 min (IQR -7.2 to 96.3), NS p=0.2; inclusion criteria used TTP cutpoints (<14h or DTP between catheter and peripheral)
outcome_one_line: Primary endpoint was device safety; all 15 patients survived 14-day follow-up (mortality 0%)
notes: Small interventional safety study (n=15). TTP is used as a pathogen-load surrogate for device efficacy, not as prognostic exposure; TTP cutpoints are also inclusion criteria. Mortality is 0/15. Per inclusive guidance, intervention studies reporting TTP descriptively with mortality data can be included for TTP distribution, but the cohort is tiny and TTP is contaminated by being both an inclusion criterion and a pre/post measurement on the device.

population_one_line: Adult and pediatric inpatients with Candida bloodstream infection (C. albicans n=43, C. glabrata n=27, others) at a US 355-bed teaching hospital over 2 years
ttp_reported: Mean TTP by species: C. albicans 35.3+/-18.1h, C. glabrata 80.0+/-22.4h (p<0.0001); time to species identification and time to appropriate therapy also reported
outcome_one_line: In-hospital mortality 29.2% (28/96); reported by Candida species (e.g., C. albicans 23.3%); time to appropriate therapy compared in survivors vs nonsurvivors (61.3h vs 58.6h, p=0.81)
notes: Previously excluded because TTP was descriptive by species and only time-to-appropriate-therapy (not TTP) was tested vs survival. Under inclusive criteria, candidemia cohort with TTP means+SD by species and overall mortality + per-species mortality is extractable. Pediatric patients included (~16% age <17).

population_one_line: Adults with infective endocarditis and positive blood cultures (194 of 322 IE cases) at a French referral hospital, 2016-2019
ttp_reported: Median TTP by pathogen (e.g., S. aureus 13.4h aerobic, 18.95h anaerobic); only 1 of 194 had TTP >120h; influence of prior antibiotics on TTP analyzed
outcome_one_line: No clinical outcome reported anywhere - no mortality, relapse, persistent bacteremia, or clinical failure data. Pure microbiology study assessing utility of prolonged (>5d) blood culture incubation
notes: Confirmed no-outcome on second pass. Grep for mortality/death/died/survival/relapse/clinical failure returned zero hits in clinical-outcome context. The paper's sole research question is microbiological (does prolonged incubation help diagnose IE?). Excluded under inclusive criteria as no_outcome.

population_one_line: Patients with acute brucellosis (62 with positive Brucella blood culture, 85 without) at a Saudi tertiary hospital, 2016-2019
ttp_reported: Median time to detect Brucella in BC 3 days (IQR 2-3); all positive cultures detected within 3 days of incubation using BACT/ALERT 3D
outcome_one_line: Chronic brucellosis 7% (9/147) and relapsed infection 10% (13/147); chronic brucellosis more common in bacteremic vs non-bacteremic (OR 7.25, 1.41-37.23); both outcomes are clinical endpoints meeting inclusive criteria
notes: Previously excluded because the exposure modeled was bacteremia status (not TTP). Under inclusive criteria, the BSI subgroup (n=62 Brucella-positive) has a median TTP and the cohort reports clinical outcomes (relapse, chronic brucellosis). Useful for fastidious organism TTP distribution data.

population_one_line: Adults with at least 1 CoNS-positive blood culture and >=2 BC sets (97 clinically-significant, 172 not) at a Spanish 873-bed tertiary hospital, Jan-Jun 2010
ttp_reported: TTP dichotomized <16h vs >=16h; TTP <16h was a multivariate predictor of clinical significance (OR 4.54, 1.73-11.88)
outcome_one_line: Persistent bacteraemia 37.1% in CSB vs 0.6% in non-CSB (p<0.05); CSB-vs-non-CSB classification is the primary outcome; mortality not formally tabulated for this cohort but persistent bacteremia is
notes: Previously excluded because the primary outcome was CDC/NHSN clinical-significance classification rather than mortality. Under inclusive criteria, persistent bacteremia (an accepted clinical outcome) is reported stratified by CSB groups; TTP <16h is reported as cutpoint with effect on CSB. A descriptive 2x2 of TTP <16h vs persistent bacteremia may be computable from supplied tables.

population_one_line: Immunocompromised (hematologic malignancy, solid tumor, immunosuppressive therapy) critically ill adults with candidemia in 3 French ICUs, 2002-2017
ttp_reported: Median delay to blood culture positivity 3 days (range 1-6 in IQR 2-4); reported descriptively for the cohort; not entered in univariate or multivariate mortality analyses
outcome_one_line: Hospital mortality 60%; ICU mortality reported; multivariate predictors were vasopressors (HR 1.8), mechanical ventilation (HR 2.0), allogenic SCT (HR 2.5)
notes: Previously excluded because TTP not modeled vs mortality. Under inclusive criteria, immunocompromised candidemia cohort with TTP summary statistic (median 3d, IQR 2-4) and hospital mortality (60%) both reported. Useful for candidemia TTP distribution + mortality rate in a high-risk subgroup.

population_one_line: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 14 controlled studies comparing T2MR vs blood culture for diagnosing BSI; no original patient cohort
ttp_reported: Pooled mean difference in time to detection T2MR vs BC = -81h (p<0.001); not a TTP-of-bacteremia summary in an original cohort
outcome_one_line: Pooled mortality T2MR 28.9% vs BC 29.9% (RR 1.02, p=0.86); a diagnostic-method comparison, not TTP vs outcome
notes: Meta-analysis/systematic review without original cohort data (wrong_design). The TTP comparison is between two diagnostic methods (T2MR vs BC) used as a benchmark for device performance; per instructions, microbiology methods studies that report TTP as a benchmark with patient outcomes only as a diagnostic-arm comparison should be excluded. Pooled estimates from secondary studies would also duplicate primary studies already in the pool.
